content_voiceover: Same diagram, but now written in Arabic numerals instead of Roman numerals, seven, eight and nine up top, ten and five in the middle, and two at the bottom. Coagulation factors get written both ways in the literature and on board exams, so it's worth being comfortable converting between them instantly. The layout hasn't changed, factor seven still stands apart as the initiator paired with tissue factor, factors eight and nine still come together as the intrinsic tenase complex that activates factor ten, and factors five and ten still form the prothrombinase complex that converts factor two into thrombin. The point of showing it twice is really just repetition, so that whether a question stem says factor eight or factor VIII, you immediately know it belongs in the tenase complex, and whether it says factor two or prothrombin, you know it's the prothrombinase substrate.
keypoints: Coagulation factors are written interchangeably as Roman or Arabic numerals
Factor 7 triggers initiation with tissue factor
Factors 8 and 9 form intrinsic tenase, activating factor 10
Factors 5 and 10 form prothrombinase, activating factor 2 to thrombin
Practice converting notation quickly for exam question stems
keypoint_voiceover: Same complexes, now in Arabic numerals, seven, eight, nine up top, ten and five in the middle, two at the bottom. Whether a question uses Roman or Arabic numbering, factors eight and nine mean intrinsic tenase, and five with ten mean prothrombinase acting on factor two. Get fluent switching between the two notations.
